```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Standing et al. (2018) studied intravenous ceftriaxone and oral metronidazole
in Kenyan infants and young children hospitalised with complicated severe acute
malnutrition (SAM), as the pharmacokinetic stage of the FLACSAM trial. The two
drugs were modelled separately, so the paper contributes two models:

* `Standing_2018_ceftriaxone` -- three-compartment model for **unbound**
  ceftriaxone, with total ceftriaxone in the central compartment and the
  unbound concentration derived from instantaneous saturable binding whose
  capacity depends on serum albumin.
* `Standing_2018_metronidazole` -- one-compartment parent and metabolite
  model in which hydroxymetronidazole is formed both on first pass and from
  circulating metronidazole through a well-stirred liver model.

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Standing_2018_ceftriaxone"))$reference`
* Ceftriaxone model: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Standing_2018_ceftriaxone"))$description`
* Metronidazole model: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Standing_2018_metronidazole"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/cpt.1078> (open access, PMC6282491)

# Population

Eighty-one children aged 2-45 months (median 14 months; weight 2.53-10.9 kg,
median 5.88 kg; 46 girls) with complicated SAM were enrolled at three Kenyan
centres (Standing 2018 Table 1). SAM was defined as kwashiorkor, a mid-upper-arm
circumference below 11.5 cm (11 cm at 1-5 months) or a weight-for-height
Z-score below -3. Children received ceftriaxone 50 mg/kg (100 mg/kg if
meningitis was suspected) as a daily intravenous bolus and metronidazole
7.5 mg/kg every 8 h as an oral suspension. Each child gave a pre-dose sample
and three post-dose samples randomised to early (5 min, 30 min, 1 h), middle
(2, 4, 8 h) and late (24, 48, 72 h) times. Eighty children contributed to the
ceftriaxone analysis and 69 to the metronidazole analysis. Nutritional oedema
was common (grades 0/1/2/3 = 45/12/14/9 in the ceftriaxone analysis) and
oedematous children were heavier. Serum albumin had a median of 33.75 g/L
(range 7-57) and serum creatinine a median of 21 umol/L (range 4-178).

The same information is available programmatically:

```{r population}
str(rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Standing_2018_ceftriaxone"))$population[c("n_subjects", "age_range", "weight_median")])
str(rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Standing_2018_metronidazole"))$population[c("n_subjects", "age_range", "weight_median")])
```

# Source trace

All structure and final estimates come from the NONMEM control streams in the
Supplementary Material (section 2.1 for ceftriaxone, section 2.2 for
metronidazole). The metronidazole estimates are also printed as the "original"
row of the initial-estimate perturbation table in section 3.2. Every `ini()`
value carries an in-file comment to its source.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|

| `lvc` (total central volume V1) | 14.4644 L | Stream THETA(2); Table 2 'V1' 14.46 |
| `lq` (Q2) | 0.933031 L/h | Stream THETA(3); Table 2 unlabelled row 0.93 |
| `lvp` (V2) | 6.05411 L | Stream THETA(4); Table 2 value 6.05 |
| `lq2` (Q3) | 29.9815 L/h | Stream THETA(5); Table 2 value 29.98 |
| `lvp2` (V3) | 19.2606 L | Stream THETA(6); Table 2 value 19.26 |
| `lbmax_pb` (Bmax) | 69.7743 mg/L | Stream THETA(7); Table 2 value 69.77 |
| `lkd_pb` (Kd) | 22.8853 mg/L | Stream THETA(8); Table 2 value 22.89; Discussion 'Kd of 22.9 mg/L' |

| `pma50_cl`, `h_pma_cl` | 47.7 weeks, 3.4 (fixed) | Stream `$PK`; Rhodin 2009 (paper ref 10) |

# Virtual cohort

The individual data are not public. The virtual children below follow the
Table 1 marginal distributions: age log-normal around 15 months within
2-45 months, weight increasing with age around the 5.88 kg median within
2.53-10.9 kg, oedema grade drawn with the Table 1 frequencies, albumin and
creatinine drawn around their medians within the observed ranges, and
haematocrit taken as three times a haemoglobin drawn around 9 g/dL. Every
child is assumed born at term, so postmenstrual age is postnatal age plus 40
weeks. Values outside a range are redrawn rather than clamped. The same 200
children are reused in every dose arm, with disjoint `id` ranges.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20180323)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20180323)

redraw <- function(n, draw, lo, hi) {
  x <- draw(n)
  bad <- x < lo | x > hi
  while (any(bad)) {
    x[bad] <- draw(sum(bad))
    bad <- x < lo | x > hi
  }
  x
}

n_sub <- 200
age_mo <- redraw(n_sub, function(n) exp(rnorm(n, log(15), 0.7)), 2, 45)
# Weight follows age; children outside the observed 2.53-10.9 kg are redrawn.
wt <- 5.88 * (age_mo / 15)^0.35 * exp(rnorm(n_sub, 0, 0.15))
bad <- wt < 2.53 | wt > 10.9
while (any(bad)) {
  wt[bad] <- 5.88 * (age_mo[bad] / 15)^0.35 * exp(rnorm(sum(bad), 0, 0.15))
  bad <- wt < 2.53 | wt > 10.9
}
grade <- sample(0:3, n_sub, replace = TRUE, prob = c(45, 12, 14, 9))
hgb <- redraw(n_sub, function(n) rnorm(n, 9, 1.6), 4.4, 12.8)

cohort <- tibble(
  sid = seq_len(n_sub),
  WT = wt,
  AGE = age_mo / 12,
  PAGE = age_mo * 4.35 + 40,
  ALB = redraw(n_sub, function(n) rnorm(n, 33.75, 8), 7, 57),
  CREAT = redraw(n_sub, function(n) exp(rnorm(n, log(21), 0.6)), 4, 178),
  HCT = 3 * hgb,
  DIS_EDEMA = as.integer(grade > 0),
  DIS_EDEMA_GE2 = as.integer(grade > 1)
)
stopifnot(all(cohort$DIS_EDEMA_GE2 <= cohort$DIS_EDEMA))
summary(cohort[, c("WT", "AGE", "ALB", "CREAT", "HCT")])
```

```{r event-helpers}
# Doses and observation rows for one arm. Observations sit on the central
# state with dvid = 1; the algebraic outputs (Cc, Cu, Cc_2oh) come back as
# columns on every observation row.
make_arm <- function(cohort, regimen, dose_mgkg, cmt_dose, dose_times, obs_times, id_offset) {
  doses <- tidyr::crossing(cohort, time = dose_times) |>
    mutate(evid = 1L, cmt = cmt_dose, amt = dose_mgkg * WT, dvid = NA_integer_)
  obs <- tidyr::crossing(cohort, time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, cmt = "central", amt = 0, dvid = 1L)
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    mutate(id = sid + id_offset, regimen = regimen) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
    select(id, time, evid, cmt, amt, dvid, regimen, everything(), -sid)
}
```

# Ceftriaxone

## Unbound fraction versus total concentration and albumin

The unbound concentration is the positive root of
`Cc = Cu + Bmax Cu / (Kd + Cu)`. The plot reproduces the model curves of
Supplementary Figure S10.

```{r fu-curve}
mod_cef <- readModelDb("Standing_2018_ceftriaxone")
ui_cef <- rxode2::rxode(mod_cef)
stopifnot(is.null(ui_cef$linCmt))
th <- setNames(ui_cef$iniDf$est, ui_cef$iniDf$name)

fu_grid <- tidyr::crossing(ALB = c(15, 25, 33.75, 45), Cc = exp(seq(log(1), log(500), length.out = 200))) |>
  mutate(
    bmax = exp(th[["lbmax_pb"]]) * (ALB / 33.75)^th[["e_alb_bmax_pb"]],
    kd = exp(th[["lkd_pb"]]),
    Cu = 0.5 * ((Cc - bmax - kd) + sqrt((Cc - bmax - kd)^2 + 4 * kd * Cc)),
    fu = Cu / Cc
  )
# The root satisfies the binding equation it was derived from.
stopifnot(max(abs(fu_grid$Cu + fu_grid$bmax * fu_grid$Cu / (fu_grid$kd + fu_grid$Cu) - fu_grid$Cc) / fu_grid$Cc) < 1e-8)

ggplot(fu_grid, aes(Cc, fu, colour = factor(ALB))) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Total ceftriaxone (mg/L)", y = "Fraction unbound", colour = "Albumin (g/L)",
    caption = "Replicates the model curves of Supplementary Figure S10 of Standing 2018."
  )
```

At low concentrations the unbound fraction tends to `Kd / (Kd + Bmax)`, about
0.25 at the median albumin of 33.75 g/L, and rises towards 1 as binding
saturates.

## Concentration-time profiles under the study regimen

```{r cef-study}
obs_72 <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 72, by = 0.5), 0.083)))
ev_cef_study <- make_arm(cohort, "50 mg/kg q24h", 50, "central", c(0, 24, 48), obs_72, 0L)
sim_cef_study <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_cef, ev_cef_study, keep = "regimen", returnType = "data.frame")

sim_cef_study |>
  select(id, time, Total = Cc, Unbound = Cu) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Total, Unbound), names_to = "analyte", values_to = "conc") |>
  group_by(analyte, time) |>
  summarise(
    p05 = quantile(conc, 0.05), p50 = median(conc), p95 = quantile(conc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, p50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~analyte) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time after first dose (h)", y = "Ceftriaxone (mg/L)",
    caption = "Median and 90% interval; compare with Figure 1 (total and unbound VPC) of Standing 2018."
  )
```

## Mass balance of unbound clearance

Only unbound drug is cleared, so after a single bolus the unbound AUC to
infinity times the individual unbound clearance must equal the dose. This holds
whatever the binding parameters are, which makes it a check of the ODE wiring.

```{r cef-mass-balance}
typ_child <- tibble(
  sid = 1L, WT = 5.88, AGE = 15 / 12, PAGE = 15 * 4.35 + 40, ALB = 33.75,
  CREAT = 21, HCT = 27, DIS_EDEMA = 0L, DIS_EDEMA_GE2 = 0L
)
mod_cef_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod_cef)
obs_long <- sort(unique(c(0, exp(seq(log(0.01), log(480), length.out = 400)))))
ev_mb <- make_arm(typ_child, "50 mg/kg single", 50, "central", 0, obs_long, 0L)
sim_mb <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_cef_typ, ev_mb, keep = "regimen", returnType = "data.frame",
                          atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-10) |>
  mutate(id = 1L) # a one-subject solve returns no id column
nca_mb <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(bind_rows(sim_mb |> select(id, time, Cu), tibble(id = 1, time = 0, Cu = 0)) |>
                     distinct(id, time, .keep_all = TRUE), Cu ~ time | id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(ev_mb |> filter(evid == 1) |> select(id, time, amt), amt ~ time | id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, aucinf.obs = TRUE),
  options = list(auc.method = "lin up/log down")
))
aucu_inf <- as.data.frame(nca_mb$result) |> filter(PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs") |> pull(PPORRES)
ratio_mb <- sim_mb$cl[1] * aucu_inf / (50 * 5.88)
ratio_mb
stopifnot(abs(ratio_mb - 1) < 0.02)
```

## Fraction of time above MIC (Figure 3)

The paper simulated single doses of 50, 80 and 100 mg/kg and reported
percentiles of the fraction of the first 24 h with unbound ceftriaxone above
the MIC. The median curve was digitised by the maintainers from Figure 3 at
MIC 4 and 8 mg/L (at MIC 2 mg/L and below it is flat at 1).

```{r cef-ftmic}
obs_24 <- seq(0, 24, by = 0.05)
cef_doses <- c(50, 80, 100)
ev_cef_ft <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(cef_doses), function(i) {
  make_arm(cohort, paste0(cef_doses[i], " mg/kg"), cef_doses[i], "central", 0, obs_24, (i - 1L) * n_sub)
}))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(ev_cef_ft[, c("id", "time", "evid")]))
sim_cef_ft <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_cef, ev_cef_ft, keep = "regimen", returnType = "data.frame")

mics <- c(0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8)
ft_cef <- sim_cef_ft |>
  filter(time > 0) |>
  tidyr::crossing(MIC = mics) |>
  group_by(regimen, id, MIC) |>
  summarise(ft = mean(Cu > MIC), .groups = "drop")

ft_cef_pct <- ft_cef |>
  group_by(regimen, MIC) |>
  summarise(
    p05 = quantile(ft, 0.05), p10 = quantile(ft, 0.10),
    p20 = quantile(ft, 0.20), p50 = median(ft), .groups = "drop"
  )

ft_cef_pct |>
  pivot_longer(p05:p50, names_to = "percentile", values_to = "ft") |>
  mutate(regimen = factor(regimen, levels = paste(cef_doses, "mg/kg"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(MIC, ft, linetype = percentile)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 2, colour = "grey60") +
  scale_x_continuous(trans = "log2", breaks = mics) +
  facet_wrap(~regimen) +
  labs(
    x = "MIC (mg/L)", y = "Fraction time > MIC", linetype = "Percentile",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 3 of Standing 2018."
  )
```

```{r cef-ftmic-compare}
fig3 <- tribble(
  ~regimen,    ~MIC, ~published,
  "50 mg/kg",  4,    0.80,
  "50 mg/kg",  8,    0.55,
  "80 mg/kg",  4,    0.93,
  "80 mg/kg",  8,    0.68,
  "100 mg/kg", 4,    0.99,
  "100 mg/kg", 8,    0.74
)

# Deterministic typical child (median covariates, no oedema) for the
# structural gate; the cohort median is shown alongside.
ev_cef_typ <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(cef_doses), function(i) {
  make_arm(typ_child, paste0(cef_doses[i], " mg/kg"), cef_doses[i], "central", 0, obs_24, i - 1L)
}))
ft_cef_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_cef_typ, ev_cef_typ, keep = "regimen", returnType = "data.frame") |>
  filter(time > 0) |>
  tidyr::crossing(MIC = c(4, 8)) |>
  group_by(regimen, MIC) |>
  summarise(typical = mean(Cu > MIC), .groups = "drop")

cmp_fig3 <- fig3 |>
  left_join(ft_cef_typ, by = c("regimen", "MIC")) |>
  left_join(ft_cef_pct |> select(regimen, MIC, cohort_median = p50), by = c("regimen", "MIC"))

cmp_fig3 |>
  rename(
    "Dose" = regimen, "MIC (mg/L)" = MIC, "Figure 3 median" = published,
    "Typical child" = typical, "Virtual-cohort median" = cohort_median
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Unbound ceftriaxone fraction of 0-24 h above the MIC.")

stopifnot(
  # Typical-value solve: a mis-transcribed CL, V1, Bmax or Kd moves these by
  # well over 0.1.
  all(abs(cmp_fig3$typical - cmp_fig3$published) < 0.08),
  # Cohort centre: depends on the virtual cohort, so a wider band.
  all(abs(cmp_fig3$cohort_median - cmp_fig3$published) < 0.12)
)
```

The Discussion states that at 50 mg/kg more than 95% of children have unbound
concentrations above 2 mg/L for at least half the interval, and that 80 mg/kg
raises the 5th percentile above 60% of the interval:

```{r cef-claims}
ft_cef_pct |>
  filter(MIC == 2) |>
  select(regimen, p05, p10, p20) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Lower percentiles of fraction time above 2 mg/L.")
```

## Covariate effects (Figure 5a and 5c)

Figure 5 reports the proportion of simulated children reaching 50% of the
interval above 2 mg/L by oedema and by serum creatinine. The figure does not
state the dose; the study dose of 50 mg/kg is used here. These proportions sit
close to 1 and are shown for direction only.

```{r cef-fig5}
pta_cef <- ft_cef |>
  filter(regimen == "50 mg/kg", MIC == 2) |>
  mutate(sid = id) |>
  left_join(cohort, by = "sid") |>
  mutate(
    Oedema = ifelse(DIS_EDEMA == 1, ">= 1", "0"),
    Creatinine = cut(CREAT, c(0, 15, 30, 60, Inf), labels = c("<15", "15-30", "30-60", ">60"))
  )
bind_rows(
  pta_cef |> group_by(group = paste("Oedema", Oedema)) |> summarise(PTA = mean(ft >= 0.5), n = n()),
  pta_cef |> group_by(group = paste("Creatinine", Creatinine, "umol/L")) |> summarise(PTA = mean(ft >= 0.5), n = n())
) |>
  left_join(tribble(
    ~group, ~published,
    "Oedema 0", 0.99, "Oedema >= 1", 0.94,
    "Creatinine <15 umol/L", 0.94, "Creatinine 15-30 umol/L", 0.97,
    "Creatinine 30-60 umol/L", 1, "Creatinine >60 umol/L", 1
  ), by = "group") |>
  rename("Group" = group, "Simulated PTA" = PTA, "Figure 5 PTA" = published) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

## PKNCA: total and unbound exposure after the first dose

The paper reports no NCA table; the values below summarise the simulated first
24 h at each dose.

```{r cef-pknca}
cef_nca_input <- sim_cef_ft |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, regimen, Cc, Cu)
dose_cef <- ev_cef_ft |> filter(evid == 1) |> select(id, time, amt, regimen)
nca_cef <- lapply(c("Cc", "Cu"), function(v) {
  conc <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(cef_nca_input, stats::as.formula(paste(v, "~ time | regimen + id")))
  dose <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_cef, amt ~ time | regimen + id)
  res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc, dose,
    intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = 24, cmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)))
  as.data.frame(res$result) |> mutate(analyte = ifelse(v == "Cc", "Total", "Unbound"))
})
bind_rows(nca_cef) |>
  group_by(analyte, regimen, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(median = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median) |>
  rename("Analyte" = analyte, "Dose" = regimen, "Cmax (mg/L)" = cmax, "AUC0-24 (mg*h/L)" = auclast) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Median simulated ceftriaxone exposure, first 24 h.")
```

# Metronidazole and hydroxymetronidazole

## Mass balance of the parent-metabolite system

With a single oral dose, `(1 - eh)` of the dose reaches the circulation as
metronidazole and is removed by `cl + clf_2oh`; hydroxymetronidazole receives
`eh` of the dose plus the systemic formation flux and is removed by `cl_2oh`.
Both AUC identities follow from the ODEs alone.

```{r met-mass-balance}
mod_met <- readModelDb("Standing_2018_metronidazole")
ui_met <- rxode2::rxode(mod_met)
stopifnot(is.null(ui_met$linCmt))
mod_met_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod_met)
typ_met <- typ_child |> mutate(AGE = 17 / 12, PAGE = 17 * 4.35 + 40)
ev_mmb <- make_arm(typ_met, "10 mg/kg single", 10, "depot", 0, obs_long, 0L)
sim_mmb <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_met_typ, ev_mmb, keep = "regimen", returnType = "data.frame",
                           atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-10) |>
  mutate(id = 1L) # a one-subject solve returns no id column
auc_inf <- function(df, v) {
  conc <- bind_rows(df |> select(id, time, all_of(v)), tibble(id = 1, time = 0, !!v := 0)) |>
    distinct(id, time, .keep_all = TRUE)
  res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
    PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, stats::as.formula(paste(v, "~ time | id"))),
    PKNCA::PKNCAdose(ev_mmb |> filter(evid == 1) |> select(id, time, amt), amt ~ time | id),
    intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, aucinf.obs = TRUE),
    options = list(auc.method = "lin up/log down")
  ))
  as.data.frame(res$result) |> filter(PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs") |> pull(PPORRES)
}
p <- sim_mmb[1, ]
dose_mmb <- 10 * 5.88
ratio_parent <- (p$cl + p$clf_2oh) * auc_inf(sim_mmb, "Cc") / ((1 - p$eh) * dose_mmb)
ratio_metab <- p$cl_2oh * auc_inf(sim_mmb, "Cc_2oh") /
  (dose_mmb * (p$eh + (1 - p$eh) * p$clf_2oh / (p$cl + p$clf_2oh)))
c(parent = ratio_parent, metabolite = ratio_metab, extraction_ratio = p$eh,
  fraction_metabolised = p$clf_2oh / (p$clf_2oh + p$cl))
stopifnot(abs(ratio_parent - 1) < 0.02, abs(ratio_metab - 1) < 0.02)
```

The typical child's extraction ratio of about 0.013 and fraction metabolised of
about 0.6 sit close to the cohort medians the authors report (0.015 and 0.636,
Supplementary Material section 3).

## Concentration-time profiles under the study regimen

```{r met-study}
ev_met_study <- make_arm(cohort, "7.5 mg/kg q8h", 7.5, "depot", seq(0, 64, by = 8), obs_72, 0L)
sim_met_study <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_met, ev_met_study, keep = "regimen", returnType = "data.frame")

sim_met_study |>
  select(id, time, Metronidazole = Cc, Hydroxymetronidazole = Cc_2oh) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(id, time), names_to = "analyte", values_to = "conc") |>
  group_by(analyte, time) |>
  summarise(
    p05 = quantile(conc, 0.05), p50 = median(conc), p95 = quantile(conc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, p50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~analyte, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Time after first dose (h)", y = "Concentration (mg/L)",
    caption = "Median and 90% interval; compare with Figure 2 (VPC) of Standing 2018."
  )
```

Both analytes accumulate over the 72 h, as the paper notes for Figure 2.

## Twice-daily regimens (Figure 4)

The paper's target-attainment simulations assumed 10% protein binding for both
analytes and weighted hydroxymetronidazole by 0.65 for its lower activity, so
the active concentration is `0.9 Cc + 0.65 x 0.9 Cc_2oh`. Figure 4b plots
AUC:MIC; at MIC 1 mg/L this is the active AUC itself. Its median line was
digitised by the maintainers at MIC 1 mg/L for 0-24 h and 24-48 h.

The Methods say both indices were calculated for 0-24 h and 24-48 h, but the
"48 hrs" panels of Figure 4a can only have been computed over the whole
0-48 h. Their median fraction of time above 1 mg/L is about 0.99 rather than 1,
which requires the absorption lag of the first dose inside the window, and
their medians at MIC 16 mg/L (0.72, 0.75 and 0.85) are what a 0-24 h value
near 0.45 combined with near-complete coverage on the second day gives over
48 h. A 24-48 h window would put every median at 1 up to MIC 8 mg/L. The AUC
panels of Figure 4b, by contrast, match 24-48 h and not 0-48 h. The fraction of
time above the MIC is therefore computed here over 0-24 h and 0-48 h, and the
AUC over 0-24 h and 24-48 h.

```{r met-fig4}
obs_48 <- seq(0, 48, by = 0.05)
met_doses <- c(10, 12.5, 15)
ev_met_bd <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(met_doses), function(i) {
  make_arm(cohort, paste0(met_doses[i], " mg/kg BD"), met_doses[i], "depot", c(0, 12, 24, 36), obs_48, (i - 1L) * n_sub)
}))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(ev_met_bd[, c("id", "time", "evid")]))
sim_met_bd <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_met, ev_met_bd, keep = "regimen", returnType = "data.frame") |>
  mutate(Cactive = 0.9 * Cc + 0.65 * 0.9 * Cc_2oh)

ft_met <- bind_rows(
  sim_met_bd |> filter(time > 0, time <= 24) |> mutate(window = "0-24 h"),
  sim_met_bd |> filter(time > 0) |> mutate(window = "0-48 h")
) |>
  tidyr::crossing(MIC = c(1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32)) |>
  group_by(regimen, window, id, MIC) |>
  summarise(ft = mean(Cactive > MIC), .groups = "drop")

ft_met |>
  group_by(regimen, window, MIC) |>
  summarise(
    p05 = quantile(ft, 0.05), p10 = quantile(ft, 0.10),
    p20 = quantile(ft, 0.20), p50 = median(ft), .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(p05:p50, names_to = "percentile", values_to = "ft") |>
  mutate(regimen = factor(regimen, levels = paste(met_doses, "mg/kg BD"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(MIC, ft, linetype = percentile)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.9, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 8, colour = "grey60") +
  scale_x_continuous(trans = "log2", breaks = c(1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32)) +
  facet_grid(window ~ regimen) +
  labs(
    x = "MIC (mg/L)", y = "Fraction time > MIC", linetype = "Percentile",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 4a of Standing 2018."
  )
```

```{r met-fig4a-compare}
# Median line of Figure 4a, digitised by the maintainers at MIC 8 and 16 mg/L.
fig4a <- tribble(
  ~regimen,        ~window,  ~MIC, ~published,
  "10 mg/kg BD",   "0-24 h", 8,    0.91,
  "10 mg/kg BD",   "0-24 h", 16,   0.44,
  "12.5 mg/kg BD", "0-24 h", 8,    0.94,
  "12.5 mg/kg BD", "0-24 h", 16,   0.49,
  "15 mg/kg BD",   "0-24 h", 8,    0.96,
  "15 mg/kg BD",   "0-24 h", 16,   0.70,
  "10 mg/kg BD",   "0-48 h", 8,    0.96,
  "10 mg/kg BD",   "0-48 h", 16,   0.72,
  "12.5 mg/kg BD", "0-48 h", 8,    0.97,
  "12.5 mg/kg BD", "0-48 h", 16,   0.75,

)
cmp_fig4a <- fig4a |>
  left_join(
    ft_met |> group_by(regimen, window, MIC) |> summarise(cohort_median = median(ft), .groups = "drop"),
    by = c("regimen", "window", "MIC")
  )
cmp_fig4a |>
  rename("Dose" = regimen, "Window" = window, "MIC (mg/L)" = MIC,
         "Figure 4a median" = published, "Virtual-cohort median" = cohort_median) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Fraction of time with active metronidazole above the MIC.")
# At MIC 16 mg/L the median sits on the steep part of the curve, where a few

stopifnot(all(abs(cmp_fig4a$cohort_median - cmp_fig4a$published) < 0.12))
```

```{r met-pknca}
met_nca_input <- sim_met_bd |>
  filter(!is.na(Cactive)) |>
  select(id, time, regimen, Cactive)
conc_met <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(met_nca_input, Cactive ~ time | regimen + id)
dose_met <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(ev_met_bd |> filter(evid == 1) |> select(id, time, amt, regimen),
                             amt ~ time | regimen + id)
nca_met <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_met, dose_met,
  intervals = data.frame(start = c(0, 24), end = c(24, 48), auclast = TRUE)))

sim_auc <- as.data.frame(nca_met$result) |>
  mutate(window = paste0(start, "-", end, " h")) |>
  select(regimen, window, PPTESTCD, PPORRES)

fig4b <- tribble(
  ~regimen,         ~window,   ~auclast,
  "10 mg/kg BD",    "0-24 h",  315,
  "12.5 mg/kg BD",  "0-24 h",  395,
  "15 mg/kg BD",    "0-24 h",  475,
  "10 mg/kg BD",    "24-48 h", 555,
  "12.5 mg/kg BD",  "24-48 h", 700,
  "15 mg/kg BD",    "24-48 h", 840
)

cmp_met <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = sim_auc,
  reference = fig4b,
  by = c("regimen", "window"),
  units = c(auclast = "mg*h/L"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp_met, caption = "Median active AUC (0.9 metronidazole + 0.65 x 0.9 hydroxymetronidazole): virtual cohort vs Figure 4b at MIC 1 mg/L.")
```

```{r met-gate}
# Deterministic typical child for the structural gate.
ev_met_typ <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(met_doses), function(i) {
  make_arm(typ_met, paste0(met_doses[i], " mg/kg BD"), met_doses[i], "depot", c(0, 12, 24, 36), obs_48, i - 1L)
}))
trap <- function(t, y) sum(diff(t) * (head(y, -1) + tail(y, -1)) / 2)
auc_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_met_typ, ev_met_typ, keep = "regimen", returnType = "data.frame") |>
  mutate(Cactive = 0.9 * Cc + 0.65 * 0.9 * Cc_2oh) |>
  group_by(regimen) |>
  summarise(
    `0-24 h` = trap(time[time <= 24], Cactive[time <= 24]),
    `24-48 h` = trap(time[time >= 24], Cactive[time >= 24]),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(-regimen, names_to = "window", values_to = "typical") |>
  left_join(fig4b, by = c("regimen", "window")) |>
  left_join(sim_auc |> group_by(regimen, window) |> summarise(cohort = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop"),
            by = c("regimen", "window")) |>
  mutate(typical_pct = 100 * (typical / auclast - 1), cohort_pct = 100 * (cohort / auclast - 1))
knitr::kable(auc_typ, digits = 1)
stopifnot(
  # Typical-value solve: a mis-transcribed clearance, volume or ka moves the
  # first-day AUC by far more than 12%.
  all(abs(auc_typ$typical_pct) < 12),
  # Cohort centre against the digitised median.
  all(abs(auc_typ$cohort_pct) < 20)
)
```

## Covariate effect of oedema (Figure 5b)

Figure 5b reports the proportion of children with at least 90% of the time
above 8 mg/L (active concentration) at 48 h by oedema grade, taken here over
0-48 h for the reason given under Figure 4. The dose is not
stated; 12.5 mg/kg twice daily, the paper's recommendation, is used here.

```{r met-fig5}
ft_met |>
  filter(regimen == "12.5 mg/kg BD", window == "0-48 h", MIC == 8) |>
  mutate(sid = id - n_sub) |>
  left_join(cohort, by = "sid") |>
  group_by(Oedema = ifelse(DIS_EDEMA_GE2 == 1, "> 1", "<= 1")) |>
  summarise(PTA = mean(ft >= 0.9), n = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(tibble(Oedema = c("<= 1", "> 1"), published = c(0.90, 0.93)), by = "Oedema") |>
  rename("Oedema grade" = Oedema, "Simulated PTA" = PTA, "Figure 5 PTA" = published) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Table 2 of the article has misaligned rows.** From the unlabelled third
  ceftriaxone row onward, every value sits one row below its label (0.93 is Q2,
  6.05 is V2, 29.98 is Q3, 19.26 is V3, 69.77 is Bmax with its 42% IIV, 22.89
  is Kd, 0.56 is the albumin exponent, and so on), and the last two residual
  rows repeat the CL and V1 entries. The NONMEM control stream in the
  Supplementary Material gives the same numbers in an unambiguous order, the
  Discussion confirms Kd = 22.9 mg/L, and Table 2's own units for "BM" (mg/h)
  are a typographical slip for mg/L. The stream is used throughout.
- **Additive error on total ceftriaxone.** The stream estimates this variance
  (no `FIX`) at exactly 0.05, which would also be a plausible initial value.
  Table 2 does not print a usable value for this row. The stream value
  (SD 0.224 mg/L) is used as an estimate.
- **Hydroxymetronidazole additive error.** Table 2 labels its 0.01 as an SD in
  mmol/L; the stream gives the variance 0.0149 on the mg/L scale. The SD
  sqrt(0.0149) = 0.122 mg/L is used.
- **First-pass metabolite formation.** The stream doses two depots (parent with
  F = 1 - ER and metabolite with F = ER) with the same ka and lag time. The
  packaged model uses a single depot whose absorbed flux is split in the same
  proportions; the two forms are mathematically identical and need one dose
  record instead of two.
- **Metabolite mass.** Parent mass is moved to the metabolite compartment
  without a molecular-weight ratio, exactly as in the stream; the difference
  is absorbed into the apparent metabolite volume.
- **Zero-variance random effects.** The metronidazole stream lists `$OMEGA 0 FIX`
  for CL, CLM and V2 and both streams list a `$SIGMA 0 FIX` additive term for
  one analyte; these are omitted, which gives the same model.
- **Haematocrit.** The stream uses haematocrit as a fraction; the canonical
  `HCT` column is a percentage, so the model divides by 100. Haematocrit is not
  reported in the paper, so the virtual cohort uses three times a haemoglobin
  drawn around the Table 1 median of 9 g/dL.
- **Oedema.** The stream carries an ordinal grade (0-3). Ceftriaxone dichotomises
  it at any oedema (`DIS_EDEMA`) and metronidazole at grade 2 or more
  (`DIS_EDEMA_GE2`); a data set for both models carries both indicators from the
  same grade.
- **Virtual cohort.** The PTA simulations in the paper resampled the study
  children, whose individual data are not public. The cohort here follows the
  Table 1 marginals only; the correlation between oedema and weight (oedematous
  children were heavier) and between age and weight are approximate. Postmenstrual
  age assumes term birth.
- **Window of the 48-h fraction of time above the MIC.** The Methods state
  24-48 h for both indices; the Figure 4a values are only consistent with
  0-48 h (see the Figure 4 section), so 0-48 h is used for that index and for
  Figure 5b, and 24-48 h for the AUC.
- **Digitised targets.** The Figure 3, Figure 4a and Figure 4b medians were digitised by
  the maintainers from the published figure files at native resolution
  (about +/-0.01 in fraction and +/-4% in AUC). The regimens behind Figure 5
  are not stated; 50 mg/kg ceftriaxone and 12.5 mg/kg twice-daily metronidazole
  are assumed and the comparison is not used as a gate.
- The PubMed record of the article (PMID 29574688, via Europe PMC) lists no
  linked erratum or correction as of 2026-11-25.
